prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated acceptable: Column 1 gets about 72px, so all store names break 3+2 (上海徐/汇店, 南京新/街口店), cutting place names in half; the resulting two-line blocks are even and the five month columns stay equal and comfortably wide, so numbers scan cleanly, but the row headers are the weak point. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Effectively the same as A: identical 3+2 wrapping of store names (杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店), even two-line row blocks and even month columns; nothing broken, but row identity is split mid-place-name, which slows reading down the header column. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 name wrap as A and B; month columns look evenly proportioned and the numeric grid reads as a clean block, yet the header column still chops 徐汇, 西湖 and 新街口, so the row labels lose a little integrity. | another layout was rated good: The wider header column lets each name put city+district on line one (上海徐汇, 南京新街, 合肥淮河) and isolates the generic suffix 店 on line two, so the distinguishing part stays intact and the lone 店 forms a consistent vertical rhythm; the cost is slightly squeezed month columns (numbers sit closer to the rules) and a stranded single character per row, but the table scans better down the row headers. | another layout was rated poor: The header column is so narrow that names break into three lines (上海/徐汇/店, 南京/新街/口店), producing very tall, airy rows; the whole table becomes a ladder of text with the month figures floating far apart, breaking row cohesion and vertical comparison between months. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 split as A/B/C with balanced month columns; readable and consistent, but the row-header breaks fall inside place names (宁波天/一店, 合肥淮/河路店), which is the weakest aspect of an otherwise tidy grid.
another layout was rated poor: 门店 column is only about three characters wide, so every store name splits mid-word (上海徐/汇店, 杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店, 宁波天/一店), breaking the branch names readers scan by. The month columns still have spare room that should have gone to column 1. | another layout was rated good: Best balance of the compact layouts: the wider row-header column keeps most branch names intact (上海徐汇/店, 杭州西湖/店), leaving only the trailing 店 orphaned, while all four-digit figures still sit on one line. log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"展示华东区各门店2024年1—5月的月度销量，便于比较门店和月份。","reading":"读者会先沿门店列定位分店，再横向查看其月度变化；也会纵向比较同一月份各店销量。每行应保持紧凑，让门店名称与五个数值读作一个整体。","groups":["1月至5月是同类、连续的时间列，应保持相近宽度，形成便于比较的数字区域。","门店列是行标识，需要足够空间呈现区分各分店的地名。"],"keep_intact":["每个销量数值应保持在一行。","尽可能保持城市和商圈等有辨识度的名称完整。"],"may_wrap":["门店名称可换成两行；优先将通用后缀“店”放在第二行，避免把商圈名称拆开。","名称已经换成两行时，行高可以容纳第二行，无需再为单字后缀增加额外高度。"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[81,56,55,55,56,56],"idea":"优先给门店名称四个汉字的空间，月份列按各自内容的最小单行宽度分配，保住数字并改善行标识。"},{"name":"B","widths":[79,56,56,56,56,56],"idea":"让五个月份列等宽并恰好容纳最长数字，其余宽度留给门店名称，在行标识和整齐的数字区之间取得平衡。"},{"name":"C","widths":[69,58,58,58,58,58],"idea":"给五个月份列更多且相等的数字留白，以门店名称更频繁地在地名中间换行作为代价。"}]}
